articles.title: Jerry Jones won't give George Pickens the contract he wants, and his future may lie outside the Cowboys
articles.standfirst: Dallas faces a major financial decision over its star receiver, with CeeDee Lamb's contract and a rising 2027 draft prospect potentially making Pickens expendable
articles.summary: Dallas faces a major financial decision over its star receiver, with CeeDee Lamb's contract and a rising 2027 draft prospect potentially making Pickens expendable
articles.body:
G eorge Pickens has already been given a very clear answer from the Dallas Cowboys when it comes to his long-term future.

The answer is not necessarily that they do not value him. It is that paying him what he wants could create a financial problem the franchise is unwilling to accept.

Pickens is currently playing the 2026 season on the franchise tag after Dallas ended negotiations over a long-term extension before the July deadline.

The one-year agreement guarantees him $27.3 million, but it does not provide the multi-year security the receiver ultimately wants. That makes the 2027 offseason particularly important.

Pickens is coming off a career-best 2025 season in which he recorded 93 catches for 1,429 yards and nine touchdowns, earning his first Pro Bowl selection.

His production alongside CeeDee Lamb has given Dak Prescott one of the league's most dangerous receiving combinations, but Dallas has never hidden the difficulty of keeping two elite wideouts on top-of-the-market contracts. Stephen Jones has already acknowledged as much.

"The situation we have with George Pickens going alongside CeeDee. I don't know of any teams that really can pay two top receivers top of the market," Jones said.

"So, yeah. That's going to be a real difficult situation as we move forward. We've managed to figure out how we can do it for this year.

"Certainly, if everything works out the way we think it is, which CeeDee and George both have huge years again, then it'll be a bigger challenge next year. George is really wanting to put back-to-back years on top of one another so it'll help his market. And certainly I know at some point, as does every player in this league, will want to be rewarded with a long-term contract. So that certainly puts pressure on us to have a unique situation there."

Those comments were made before the current season had played out, but they explain why Pickens ' contract situation remains one of the Cowboys ' biggest looming decisions.

Lamb's existing deal averages $34 million per year, while Pickens' 2026 franchise-tag salary already represents a substantial investment. Dallas would therefore have to decide whether allocating another enormous contract to its second receiver is the best use of its resources.

Charlie Becker could give Dallas a cheaper alternative

That is where the 2027 NFL Draft enters the equation. A recent mock draft from Athlon Sports' Luke Easterling projects Dallas to select Indiana wide receiver Charlie Becker with the No. 8 overall pick.

The scenario is notable because Arch Manning is still available when the Cowboys are on the clock, yet Dallas passes on the Texas quarterback and instead selects a potential replacement for Pickens.

Manning is projected to fall to Cleveland at No. 15 in that particular projection. The Cowboys ' decision in that mock is based on the assumption that Pickens will not receive the long-term contract he is seeking and will ultimately leave Dallas.

"I don't expect the Cowboys to pay top dollar to keep George Pickens as their WR2 across from CeeDee Lamb, and if he ends up leaving in the offseason, they'll need a capable replacement," Easterling wrote.

Becker would certainly fit the profile of a player capable of replacing some of what Dallas could lose.

The Indiana wideout stands 6-foot-4 and weighs around 208 pounds, combining size with the athleticism required to threaten defenses vertically.

He produced 34 receptions for 679 yards and four touchdowns in 2025, averaging an eye-catching 20 yards per catch. His production has increased dramatically early in 2026, with 19 catches for 370 yards and six touchdowns through four games.

That is an average of 92.5 receiving yards per game, and his 19.5 yards per reception show why scouts are beginning to view him as more than just a complementary prospect.

" Becker brings an impressive blend of size (6-4, 208) and athleticism to the table, with the hands and body control to win contested-catch situations, along with a knack for making big plays in clutch moments," Easterling said.

Other early 2027 mock drafts have also placed Becker firmly in first-round territory, demonstrating how quickly his stock has risen following Indiana's national championship campaign and his impressive start to the current season.

There is, of course, still a considerable amount of football to be played before Dallas has to make this decision.

A strong 2026 season from Pickens could make it much harder for the Cowboys to let him walk. Dallas has also previously indicated that it viewed him as part of its long-term plans, even while acknowledging the financial complications.

Jerry Jones said earlier in the year that the organization had "long term plans" for Pickens, while Stephen Jones later made clear just how challenging the economics could become.

That tension could ultimately define the receiver's future.

The Cowboys can afford Pickens for 2026 because the franchise tag gives them a one-year solution. The more difficult question arrives when Pickens is able to test the market and ask Dallas to make him one of the highest-paid receivers in football.

At that point, Jerry Jones will have to choose between maintaining an elite receiving duo and spreading the money elsewhere.

A first-round talent such as Becker would not be an identical replacement for Pickens , but he could give Dallas a younger and considerably more cost-controlled alternative.

And with Prescott , Lamb and other expensive pieces already demanding significant resources, that could be enough to push Pickens toward the exit.

The Cowboys may still find a way to keep him.

The answer is not necessarily that they do not value him. It is that paying him what he wants could create a financial problem the franchise is unwilling to accept.
Pickens is currently playing the 2026 season on the franchise tag after Dallas ended negotiations over a long-term extension before the July deadline.
The one-year agreement guarantees him $27.3 million, but it does not provide the multi-year security the receiver ultimately wants. That makes the 2027 offseason particularly important.
Pickens is coming off a career-best 2025 season in which he recorded 93 catches for 1,429 yards and nine touchdowns, earning his first Pro Bowl selection.

"The situation we have with George Pickens going alongside CeeDee. I don't know of any teams that really can pay two top receivers top of the market," Jones said.
"So, yeah. That's going to be a real difficult situation as we move forward. We've managed to figure out how we can do it for this year.

"Certainly, if everything works out the way we think it is, which CeeDee and George both have huge years again, then it'll be a bigger challenge next year. George is really wanting to put back-to-back years on top of one another so it'll help his market. And certainly I know at some point, as does every player in this league, will want to be rewarded with a long-term contract. So that certainly puts pressure on us to have a unique situation there."
Those comments were made before the current season had played out, but they explain why Pickens ' contract situation remains one of the Cowboys ' biggest looming decisions.

Lamb's existing deal averages $34 million per year, while Pickens' 2026 franchise-tag salary already represents a substantial investment. Dallas would therefore have to decide whether allocating another enormous contract to its second receiver is the best use of its resources.

The scenario is notable because Arch Manning is still available when the Cowboys are on the clock, yet Dallas passes on the Texas quarterback and instead selects a potential replacement for Pickens.

Manning is projected to fall to Cleveland at No. 15 in that particular projection. The Cowboys ' decision in that mock is based on the assumption that Pickens will not receive the long-term contract he is seeking and will ultimately leave Dallas.

"I don't expect the Cowboys to pay top dollar to keep George Pickens as their WR2 across from CeeDee Lamb, and if he ends up leaving in the offseason, they'll need a capable replacement," Easterling wrote.
Becker would certainly fit the profile of a player capable of replacing some of what Dallas could lose.
The Indiana wideout stands 6-foot-4 and weighs around 208 pounds, combining size with the athleticism required to threaten defenses vertically.

He produced 34 receptions for 679 yards and four touchdowns in 2025, averaging an eye-catching 20 yards per catch. His production has increased dramatically early in 2026, with 19 catches for 370 yards and six touchdowns through four games.

That tension could ultimately define the receiver's future.

articles.title: Calls for NFL to investigate Joey Porter Jr. following suspicious move by the Cowboys
articles.standfirst: The cornerback is ready to play days after leaving Pittsburgh
articles.summary: The cornerback is ready to play days after leaving Pittsburgh
articles.body:
J oey Porter Jr. is preparing to make his Dallas Cowboys debut against the Houston Texans , and the timing has triggered a fresh wave of suspicion among frustrated Pittsburgh Steelers fans.

Porter missed Pittsburgh’s first three games while dealing with a back injury and conditioning concerns, yet he arrived in Dallas this week without an injury designation and is expected to play Sunday.

That abrupt change has led some supporters to demand the NFL look into whether Porter was truly unable to play for the Steelers , particularly after months of failed contract negotiations preceded his trade.

Porter had been listed with a back problem throughout training camp and remained inactive through the opening three weeks, although his practice participation increased before the trade.

NFL.com reported that his final Steelers designation combined “not injury related/conditioning/back,” while Porter himself said in late September that he was still working toward being “100 percent.”

The Steelers finally moved the 26-year-old to Dallas for a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-round selection after failing to reach agreement on a new contract.

Porter is entering the final year of his rookie deal, turning what had become a prolonged Pittsburgh standoff into an immediate fresh start.

Fans question sudden Cowboys availability

The sight of Porter practising with Dallas and immediately moving toward game action predictably drew reaction online.

“NFL should investigate Joey Porter Jr and his agent for faking a back injury,” one Steelers-focused account wrote, while another fan claimed, “He blatantly faked an injury.”

Others were far less convinced, pointing out that proving an injury was fabricated would require far more than frustration over the timing of his return.

Dallas ’ own plan also cuts against the idea that Porter is simply stepping straight back into a full workload, with reports indicating the Cowboys intend to limit his snaps against Houston.

Head coach Brian Schottenheimer said Porter impressed immediately but stressed Dallas still wanted to see consecutive strong practices before committing to his role.

“Go out there and do what he did yesterday, which was really impressive,” Schottenheimer said, adding that communication and understanding of the defense were also important considerations.

Dallas also doesn't expect Porter to play every defensive snap in his first appearance, with the coaching staff preparing a specific package for him.

That cautious approach is consistent with a player returning after a lengthy absence rather than one who has been playing and training normally throughout the opening month.

Porter gets fresh start with Cowboys

The Cowboys need help immediately after injuries hit their secondary, making Porter an attractive addition regardless of the circumstances surrounding his exit from Pittsburgh.

Dallas sent significant draft capital to acquire a cornerback who has started 41 NFL games and recorded 31 passes defended through his first three seasons.

Porter now has an opportunity to shift attention away from the contract dispute and questions surrounding his back by performing against Houston. His return may continue to frustrate Steelers fans, but calls for an investigation remain based on suspicion rather than evidence.

articles.title: “That goes for you as well, Dak”: Harsh advice for Sarah Jane Ramos and Dak Prescott after cheating allegations
articles.standfirst: The advice came days after Ramos accused the Dallas quarterback of repeated infidelity during their relationship
articles.summary: The advice came days after Ramos accused the Dallas quarterback of repeated infidelity during their relationship
articles.body:
The end of Dak Prescott and Sarah Jane Ramos ’ engagement has become increasingly public, but Mike Fisher believes the focus now needs to move away from accusations and toward parenting.

Ramos recently responded to online speculation that she was pregnant by saying she wasn't expecting and was happier since leaving what she described as a relationship marked by repeated cheating.

“Not pregnant!! Just very thick, eating again, and happier than I've been in a long time!” Ramos wrote.

She then added that this was “usually what happens when you aren’t getting cheated on repeatedly and finally leave a situation that makes you unhappy.”

Children should come before the breakup

Eleven days after Ramos ’ comments, Fisher offered advice aimed at both sides.

“As a father of two sons who are the product of a divorce, I'm offering sincerity and not sarcasm as I serve up some unsolicited ‘broken-home’ advice to Sarah Jane Ramos,” Fisher wrote. “It's not about you. Oh, and Dak Prescott, that goes for you as well.”

His message centered on the former couple’s daughters, MJ and Aurora.

“Dallas Cowboys quarterback Prescott and his ex-fiancée have two baby daughters who deserve to be raised by parents who are wise and generous enough to prioritize the needs of the kids,” Fisher said. “Regardless of the pain felt by the parents.”

Prescott and Ramos began dating in 2023 and welcomed MJ in February 2024 before Aurora was born in May 2025.

Their wedding had been scheduled for April, but the engagement ended in March during a joint bachelor-bachelorette trip in the Bahamas. A message reportedly sent to wedding guests said they had made “the very difficult decision to cancel our wedding.”

Daughters remain Ramos' priority

Despite the public nature of the split, Ramos has also framed her daughters as the center of her life.

Last week, she shared beach photos with both girls and wrote: “A whole lot of love held together by Faith. Our very solid little family. My girls, my rocks. Maybe the greatest thing I ever built was us.”

That message lines up closely with Fisher ’s broader point. His comments were not about deciding who was at fault in the breakup, nor were they a defense of either side. They were about what comes next.

Prescott and Ramos remain tied together through their children, regardless of how their relationship ended. The cheating claim may continue to attract attention, especially while Prescott remains one of the NFL’s most visible players.

articles.title: Haley Cavinder appeared at the Cowboys-Texans game with a very special message for Jake Ferguson
articles.standfirst: What did she say?
articles.summary: What did she say?
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys returned to the United States on October 4 to face the Houston Texans at NRG Stadium , following a Week 3 that ended with a 34-31 loss to the Baltimore Ravens in Brazil . Haley Cavinder could not join Jake Ferguson on that trip, but this time she was in Houston to watch him play.

Before the game, Haley shared part of her trip on a private jet on Instagram . But it was her arrival at the stadium that ended up catching attention, thanks to one detail in the outfit she chose that had a very personal connection to her husband.

What did Haley Cavinder wear?

Haley wore a white shirt tied into a top, featuring the blue letters “#sWAG” across the front . She paired it with denim jeans, a brown belt, beige cowboy boots and a Cowboys cap.

The outfit had a style of its own and fit right in with the atmosphere surrounding the game, but one accessory featured a direct reference to Jake.

The buckle was personalized with Jake Ferguson’s No. 87 , the word “Ferg” and a star in the center.

It was a small detail, but one with a clear message: Haley found a way to include Jake in a look that still felt completely like her own.

What happened in the game?

While Haley watched from the stands, Dallas had to come from behind in a game that Houston controlled for much of the afternoon. The Texans dominated the first half, while the Cowboys could only respond with two Brandon Aubrey field goals, sending Dallas into halftime down 16-6 .

The Cowboys’ comeback came after the break. Javonte Williams scored three touchdowns, including one that helped Dallas take a 27-23 lead in the fourth quarter .

Houston quickly answered. With about two and a half minutes remaining, Woody Marks scored a rushing touchdown to put the Texans back in front, 30-27 .

Then came Dallas’ final response. Dak Prescott led an 11-play, 74-yard drive that included a crucial fourth-down conversion . The possession ended when Prescott found CeeDee Lamb for a 12-yard touchdown with 40 seconds left on the clock.

The score put Dallas ahead 34-30 , and Houston could not complete the comeback on its final possession. The Cowboys secured their second win of the season and improved to 2-2.

When do the Cowboys play again?

Dallas will have little time to enjoy the win, as the Cowboys return to the field on Thursday, October 8, when they host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at AT&T Stadium .

And after seeing the detail Haley chose to bring Jake into her game-day look in Houston, her next appearance alongside him could come with another outfit surprise.

articles.title: The Dallas Cowboys are generating excitement, and the boldest prediction still stands: “They're going to win their division”
articles.standfirst: Dallas erased another late deficit against Houston, giving Mike Greenberg fresh reason to believe his preseason NFC East prediction can become reality
articles.summary: Dallas erased another late deficit against Houston, giving Mike Greenberg fresh reason to believe his preseason NFC East prediction can become reality
articles.body:
Mike Greenberg is refusing to abandon his preseason prediction about the Dallas Cowboys .

After a turbulent opening month, Dallas finally produced the type of late-game response that could make Greenberg's prediction look considerably less ambitious.

The Cowboys rallied from behind to defeat the Houston Texans 34-30 on Sunday, improving to 2-2 and keeping themselves firmly within the NFC East race.

Greenberg , the ESPN "Get Up!" host who backed Dallas to win the division before the season, immediately doubled down following the dramatic victory.

“This time Dak throws the touchdown and the defense gets the stop at the end. What a difference a week makes. #Cowboys are gonna win that division,” he shared.

The comment referenced the Cowboys' previous game, a 30-27 overtime loss to the Baltimore Ravens in Brazil, when Dallas had a chance to close out the game but ultimately watched its lead disappear. Against Houston, the ending was very different.

Dak Prescott engineered an 11-play, 74-yard drive in just one minute and 43 seconds before connecting with CeeDee Lamb for the decisive 12-yard touchdown. It was Prescott's 27th career game-winning drive, and the victory prevented Dallas from slipping below .500 after four games.

Lamb was extraordinary throughout the afternoon. He finished with a career-high 17 receptions for 189 yards and the game-winning touchdown, repeatedly giving Prescott a reliable target when Dallas desperately needed to move the football.

The Cowboys also received a major contribution from Javonte Williams , who scored three rushing touchdowns after halftime as Dallas overcame a 10-point deficit.

Dallas still has plenty of work to do in the NFC East

Greenberg's prediction remains far from a certainty, however.

The Cowboys currently sit behind the New York Giants , who are 3-1, while Dallas and the Philadelphia Eagles are both 2-2. Washington is 1-3. That leaves the NFC East unusually open after four weeks, with Dallas only one game behind first place.

The victory over Houston was especially important because the Cowboys had to demonstrate that they could finish a close game after last week's collapse against Baltimore.

Prescott did exactly that, although the quarterback was quick to caution against interpreting one victory as proof that every problem has disappeared.

"There's nothing like winning," Prescott said. "I want to say it fixes all the problems, but it doesn't. It makes you feel good at least for a day or so. But at this point, we got to turn the page and get ready for Thursday. We can't sit here and have some winning hangover so early in the season."

That mindset could be crucial because Dallas has almost no time to enjoy the victory.

The Cowboys return to action Thursday night against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at AT&T Stadium. The game kicks off at 8:15 p.m. ET, giving Dallas only a few days to recover from the trip to Houston.

Head coach Brian Schottenheimer nevertheless believes the way his players responded says something significant about the group.

“Speaks to the type of young men we have in that room,” Schottenheimer said of his team’s effort. “These guys are a special group of young men that truly do love each other. The brotherhood is real. There was never finger pointing one way or the other. They just went back to work. We’re going to do it again in however many days… Can’t wait.”

Schottenheimer also pushed back against the idea that Sunday's game was a must-win, particularly given the circumstances surrounding the schedule.

“I wanted this game. I didn’t think we needed this game. Rio doesn’t define us as a football team…” Schottenheimer said.

“But I wanted this game. Why? Because these guys came back off a ten hour trip, the Ravens I think played at home today, we played on the road. We play Thursday night. We’ll play anybody anywhere. And we’re looking forward to that. But Rio had nothing to do with this game, this game stood by itself.”

The Cowboys ' comeback does not eliminate their defensive concerns. Houston still produced 30 points, and the Cowboys surrendered several big plays before tightening up late.

Dallas will need considerably more consistency if it wants to turn a 2-2 start into a division title. Still, the NFC East is hardly running away from them.

The Giants currently have the best record, but Dallas has Prescott , Lamb and an offense capable of producing explosive stretches. The win in Houston also demonstrated something the Cowboys desperately needed after their loss in Brazil: they can make the final drive count.

For Greenberg, that may be enough to keep the preseason prediction alive.

There are 13 games still remaining, beginning with Thursday's matchup against Tampa Bay. If Dallas continues finding ways to win close games, the prediction that initially looked bold could become increasingly realistic as the season develops.

articles.title: Cowboys offense is putting up numbers seen from conference championship teams as Dallas chases an end to its 30-year drought
articles.standfirst: Since 2010, the Cowboys are the only team in the NFC that hasn't reached the championship game
articles.summary: Since 2010, the Cowboys are the only team in the NFC that hasn't reached the championship game
articles.body:
What a necessary win for the Dallas Cowboys by defeating the Houston Texans on the road 34-30 with an amazing exhibition from CeeDee Lamb who caught a career-high 17 passes for 189 yards , including Dak Prescott’s game-winning touchdown as the Dallas Cowboys rallied to stun the Texans and evened their record at 2-2 , while the Texans dropped to 0-4 .

Lamb finished one catch shy of the franchise record for receptions in a game, set by Jason Witten in 2012 . Prescott finished 32-of-45 for 335 yards and a touchdown while Javonte Williams scored three touchdowns on the ground, all in the second half, as Dallas has scored 30+ points in its last three games.

Cowboys Offense Paces Elite Company Matching Historic Conference Finalists

The Dallas offense led by Prescott has looked sharp all year, with the team averaging 3.39 points per drive across the first four games of the season.

This stellar average ranks No. 5 among all NFL offenses through the first four games of a season since 2000, as pointed out by Anthony Dabbundo. Obviously, there are still 13 games remaining on the schedule, but this milestone highlights the explosive capability Dallas has shown.

While Dallas is currently mired in a two-year playoff drought and a glaring 30-year streak of failing to reach the NFC Championship Game since winning their last Super Bowl, the longest active drought in the conference, where every other team has appeared in the title game at least once since 2010 , historical trends offer immense encouragement.

As a strong positive omen, every single team sitting alongside Dallas in the 1-6 range of this specific points-per-drive category ultimately advanced to their respective Conference Championship Game , led by the 2020 Green Bay Packers (3.67) , the 2024 Washington Commanders (3.56) , and the 2021 Kansas City Chiefs (3.53) .

Although all three of those historical clubs fell short in the conference round, merely breaking through would bring immense relief to an expectant fanbase that will not tolerate another playoff-less campaign under Prescott and head coach Brian Schottenheimer .

High-Stakes Prime-Time Gauntlet Awaits for Dallas

Next up, the Cowboys host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Thursday Night Football in Week 5 before embarking on a brutal back-to-back road trip against the Green Bay Packers on Sunday Night Football in Week 6 , followed by the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday Night Football in Week 7 .

If the Cowboys can keep this high-octane offense rolling, securing a winning record by the start of November will be entirely within reach, providing a vital cushion for a significantly tougher slate down the stretch.

Prescott finished 32-of-45 for 335 yards and a touchdown while Javonte Williams scored three touchdowns on the ground, all in the second half, as Dallas has scored 30+ points in its last three games.
Cowboys Offense Paces Elite Company Matching Historic Conference Finalists
The Dallas offense led by Prescott has looked sharp all year, with the team averaging 3.39 points per drive across the first four games of the season.

This stellar average ranks No. 5 among all NFL offenses through the first four games of a season since 2000, as pointed out by Anthony Dabbundo. Obviously, there are still 13 games remaining on the schedule, but this milestone highlights the explosive capability Dallas has shown.

While Dallas is currently mired in a two-year playoff drought and a glaring 30-year streak of failing to reach the NFC Championship Game since winning their last Super Bowl, the longest active drought in the conference, where every other team has appeared in the title game at least once since 2010 , historical trends offer immense encouragement.

As a strong positive omen, every single team sitting alongside Dallas in the 1-6 range of this specific points-per-drive category ultimately advanced to their respective Conference Championship Game , led by the 2020 Green Bay Packers (3.67) , the 2024 Washington Commanders (3.56) , and the 2021 Kansas City Chiefs (3.53) .

Although all three of those historical clubs fell short in the conference round, merely breaking through would bring immense relief to an expectant fanbase that will not tolerate another playoff-less campaign under Prescott and head coach Brian Schottenheimer .
High-Stakes Prime-Time Gauntlet Awaits for Dallas

Next up, the Cowboys host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Thursday Night Football in Week 5 before embarking on a brutal back-to-back road trip against the Green Bay Packers on Sunday Night Football in Week 6 , followed by the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday Night Football in Week 7 .

If the Cowboys can keep this high-octane offense rolling, securing a winning record by the start of November will be entirely within reach, providing a vital cushion for a significantly tougher slate down the stretch.

articles.title: Jerry Jones steps in after Cowboys player gets urgent family news during Texans win
articles.standfirst: Linebacker Shemar James left the locker room in a rush after his wife went into labor, with Jones helping arrange the trip home
articles.summary: Linebacker Shemar James left the locker room in a rush after his wife went into labor, with Jones helping arrange the trip home
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys were still celebrating a 34-30 win over the Texans when Shemar James was already on his way out of the locker room.

His wife, Erica , had gone into labor during the NFL game, instantly changing the meaning of an already emotional Sunday for the young linebacker.

Head coach Brian Schottenheimer revealed the situation after the win, initially talking about the mood around George Pickens before correcting himself.

“There’s no one more excited in that locker room right now than George Pickens,” Schottenheimer said. “Well, maybe. Shemar James’ wife is in labor, and he’ll be flying home with the Joneses. And that’s pretty cool. So, praying for an easy delivery, and God is good.”

Jones made sure James could leave immediately

The urgency became obvious in video from Dallas’ locker room. James , still wrapped in a towel, joined the team celebration only briefly before helping break the huddle and rushing away.

He had recorded two solo tackles in the victory, but football was no longer his priority once the news came through. Jones stepped in to speed up the trip home.

James was given a place on the Jones family’s flight back to Dallas rather than having to wait for the team’s normal travel schedule. A later report said Jones also arranged an escort to take the linebacker directly from the runway to the hospital.

The goal was to remove as many delays as possible. That gesture fit the moment. The Cowboys had just completed a difficult road win, but Jones understood that James had somewhere far more important to be.

Long relationship with Cowboys players

Jones has long cultivated a reputation for maintaining personal relationships with players beyond what happens on Sundays. Former offensive lineman Nate Newton has spoken about Jones standing by him after his playing career ended and legal problems followed.

“He ain’t never turned his back on me,” Newton said. “He’s always had a few kind words for me.”

Dez Bryant has also credited Jones with offering advice that extended beyond football, particularly when it came to handling money and business early in his career.

“I learned a lot of stuff from Jerry, especially with my own business,” Bryant said. “It’s just the way he inspires people.”

Jones didn't simply congratulate James after the win and leave the situation to team staff. He got directly involved, making sure the linebacker had the quickest path back to his family.

Dallas left Houston with another victory. James left with something much more important waiting for him at home.

articles.title: Michael Irvin defends Dak Prescott by calling for everyone at ESPN to be fired
articles.standfirst: Irvin delivered a fiery response after ESPN’s panel questioned Prescott’s standing against Jameis Winston
articles.summary: Irvin delivered a fiery response after ESPN’s panel questioned Prescott’s standing against Jameis Winston
articles.body:
Dak Prescott has spent much of his NFL career under a microscope, with every strong stretch and every setback feeding another round of debate about where he belongs among the league’s top quarterbacks.

Michael Irvin believes some of that criticism has become unreasonable. During a discussion on First Take, Irvin reacted sharply after the panel entertained the idea that Jameis Winston could be better than Prescott .

“You all are telling me out of your mouths, you all going to let your bodies formulate the words that come over your tongue and out your lips that you expect Jameis Winston to be better than Dak Prescott,” Irvin said. “Stop this show right now. Get rid of all of y’all right now.”

The Hall of Famer made clear that his reaction wasn't meant as a personal shot at Winston . “I’m taking Dak Prescott every time,” Irvin said.

Prescott’s current form central to Irvin’s argument

Irvin ’s defense comes with Prescott playing some of his best football of the season.

Through four games, the 33-year-old has completed 105 of 150 passes for 1,065 yards, eight touchdowns and only one interception. He ranks third in the NFL in both completions and touchdown passes.

Prescott completed 32 of 45 passes for 335 yards and a touchdown in Dallas’ 34-30 comeback victory over Houston, then led the decisive 74-yard drive that ended with a touchdown pass to CeeDee Lamb with 40 seconds remaining.

He did it while dealing with swelling in his throwing hand after it was stepped on during the game.

Prescott ’s career numbers also give Irvin plenty to point toward. He has thrown for 37,054 yards and 251 touchdowns, compared with Winston ’s 25,271 yards and 159 touchdowns.

Winston still given Giants timely lift

The comparison has gained traction because Winston has played well since taking over for Jaxson Dart , who suffered a season-ending knee injury.

Winston is 2-0 as New York’s starter, helping the Giants stabilize their season and move to 3-1.

He and Prescott also share a connection that goes back to their college days, when they were roommates at the Peyton Manning Passing Academy.

Winston has publicly supported Prescott in the years since. Still, Irvin’s broader point was about how quickly Prescott’s accomplishments can get dismissed.

Dallas may be only 2-2, but the Cowboys have scored the second-most points in the NFL, and Prescott has been one of the main reasons why.

The debate will continue as both teams move deeper into the season. Irvin, however, has already made his position impossible to misunderstand.

articles.title: Brian Schottenheimer maintains full faith in Cowboys defense despite nightmare 2026 start
articles.standfirst: Brian Schottenheimer still believes in the Cowboys defense despite a disastrous start.
articles.summary: Brian Schottenheimer still believes in the Cowboys defense despite a disastrous start.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys are 2-2 after defeating the Houston Texans 34-30 in Week 4. The team remains in the race in the NFC East , but the defense has been one of its biggest concerns early in the season. Even so, head coach Brian Schottenheimer has not lost confidence in that unit.

During a press conference on Monday , the 52-year-old coach said the defense is showing signs of improvement. For Schottenheimer , the group will eventually reach the level needed for the team to rely on it in key moments.

“I think our defense is getting better,” Schottenheimer said. “I don’t want to have to score 30 points every game to win. … But if we got to score 35 or whatever it takes to win, we’ll do that, because at some point they’re gonna bail us out and we’re gonna win a game 10-7.”

The numbers don’t tell the story

Dallas has allowed 28 points or more in three of its four games, and both of its victories came in games where the offense scored 34 or more points. Overall, the Cowboys have surrendered 112 points through the first four weeks, the fourth-highest total in the NFL.

The moves to turn things around

The front office has not stayed quiet. In addition to adding talent during the offseason, Dallas recently acquired cornerback Joey Porter Jr. in a trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers to strengthen the secondary. With so many new faces on the roster, the team may simply need time to find its defensive identity.

Dallas will have another opportunity to fix its issues in Week 5, when the Cowboys host a struggling Tampa Bay Buccaneers team in Thursday Night Football .

articles.title: Jerry Jones receives an interesting proposal: “Troy Aikman and Tony Romo have to return to the Cowboys”
articles.standfirst: With Tony Romo now out at CBS and Troy Aikman’s future in the booth under scrutiny, a return to Dallas could be worth exploring
articles.summary: With Tony Romo now out at CBS and Troy Aikman’s future in the booth under scrutiny, a return to Dallas could be worth exploring
articles.body:
Former Dallas Cowboys wide receiver Dez Bryant has presented Jerry Jones with an intriguing idea, and that is to bring franchise legends Troy Aikman and Tony Romo back into the organization.

Bryant , who made three Pro Bowls during his Cowboys career, shared his thoughts on X on October 5, writing that Aikman and Romo “need to be part of the Cowboys organization.”

His suggestion comes at an interesting time, with both former Dallas quarterbacks facing uncertainty surrounding their broadcasting futures.

Aikman remains one of the most accomplished players in Cowboys history. The Hall of Fame quarterback spent his entire 12-year NFL career in Dallas and guided the franchise to three Super Bowl victories during the 1990s. After retiring in 2001, he quickly moved into broadcasting, first with Fox before later becoming a prominent voice on ESPN.

Romo followed a similar path after ending his playing career in 2017. The four-time Pro Bowler spent all 14 of his NFL seasons with Dallas before becoming CBS Sports’ lead NFL analyst.

His nine-year run alongside Jim Nantz established him as one of the most recognizable voices in football broadcasting.

However, Romo’s broadcasting chapter has now ended. CBS Sports announced on October 2 that it had mutually agreed to part ways with the former quarterback following his leave of absence. J.J. Watt has taken over alongside Nantz and Tracy Wolfson for the remainder of the season.

Could Aikman and Romo return to Dallas?

Bryant’s proposal also arrives as Aikman has become increasingly vocal about the Cowboys’ lack of postseason success. Dallas hasn’t reached the NFC Championship Game since Aikman helped win Super Bowl XXX following the 1995 season.

Aikman recently described that prolonged drought as difficult to comprehend and said Cowboys supporters deserve better.

“Cowboys fans deserve better,” Aikman said. “I do know that. This is the Cowboys, the flagship franchise, and the fact that the Cowboys in 30 years have not made it to a championship game, let along a Super Bowl, it’s hard to fathom.”

The former quarterback also pointed toward the organization’s structure when discussing the team’s struggles. He argued that Jones ’ continued role as general manager deserves examination, particularly because the Cowboys haven’t found sustained postseason success since their championship era.

“To me, you have to make changes in how you’re doing it, if for three decades you haven’t made an NFC Championship Game,” Aikman said. “It’s just unacceptable.”

That perspective makes Bryant’s idea especially interesting. Aikman could potentially bring his experience to an advisory or football operations role, while Romo could offer insight shaped by both his playing career and nearly a decade analyzing the league from the broadcast booth.

There’s no indication that either quarterback is actually being considered for a Cowboys position. Still, Romo is now free from CBS, while Aikman’s future with ESPN could become a bigger talking point as his contract situation develops.

articles.title: Cowboys’ Michael Irvin used strip club as his “office” during interview with renowned NFL reporter
articles.standfirst: Irvin was always known as a loose cannon, and this story confirms it.
articles.summary: Irvin was always known as a loose cannon, and this story confirms it.
articles.body:
Having spent 12 seasons with the organization - the duration of his entire NFL career - and helping win three Super Bowls for the franchise, Michael Irvin is synonymous with the Dallas Cowboys . You can't tell the story of the Cowboys without mentioning Irvin.

Irvin is one of the best wide receivers to ever grace the gridiron. Yet beyond his immense talent, it's his outgoing personality that has endeared him to fans all around the nation since his playing career came to a close. From heartfelt monologues on NFL Network to riling up the crowd at Miami Hurricanes games , Irvin always leaves people something to talk about.

That was very much true during his playing days as well. Countless stories of his endeavors have made the rounds since the 1990s, and on Tuesday, Peter King dropped an amazing anecdote about Irvin to further his legacy.

Michael Irvin made Peter King interview him at a strip club

The iconic NFL reporter told the story of setting up an interview with Irvin. Irvin told King to swing by his office to do the interview. When King arrived at the scene, he ended up at a strip club, which Irvin said was "my office" .

For those who know the backstory of Irvin, this won't be surprising. But it's another feather in the cap of a truly unique personality.

articles.title: Jerry Jones unable to enjoy latest Cowboys victory after Colin Kaepernick puts him in awkward position
articles.standfirst: The former 49ers quarterback reopened a decade-old NFL debate during an appearance in Dallas
articles.summary: The former 49ers quarterback reopened a decade-old NFL debate during an appearance in Dallas
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys had barely moved on from an emotional 34-30 win over the Houston Texans when owner Jerry Jones found himself pulled back into one of the league’s most enduring controversies.

Former San Francisco 49ers quarterback Colin Kaepernick appeared in Dallas for an author event tied to his memoir, The Perilous Fight, and was asked what he would say now to Jones and others who opposed his protest during the 2016 season.

“It’s the same thing that I’ve said in the past, which is, why are you so comfortable working against black folks trying to live?” Kaepernick said. “People revealed who they were.”

His remarks brought Jones ’ stance from that period back into focus just as Dallas was trying to build momentum on the field.

Issue that changed Kaepernick's career

Kaepernick began kneeling during the national anthem in 2016 as a protest against racial injustice and police violence involving black Americans.

“We were fighting specifically against police killing black folks,” he said in Dallas. “It’s amazing to me that there’s anybody that’s like, ‘I’m against that.’”

At the time, Jones was one of the NFL’s most prominent critics of anthem demonstrations.

“There is no question the league is suffering negative effects from these protests,” Jones said in 2017.

He argued that the NFL needed to protect the strength of the league and avoid allowing protests to overshadow football. Kaepernick , however, has always maintained that the issue went beyond the sport itself.

“I am not going to stand up to show pride in a flag for a country that oppresses black people and people of color,” he said in 2016. “To me, this is bigger than football, and it would be selfish on my part to look the other way.”

Cowboys win briefly pushed aside

The timing made Kaepernick ’s comments especially awkward for Jones . Dallas had just completed a dramatic comeback victory, with Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb helping the Cowboys secure a result that gave the franchise something positive to build on.

Instead, the public conversation around Jones quickly returned to an issue he had hoped was long behind him.

Kaepernick hasn't played an NFL snap since the 2016 season, but he has remained active in social justice causes and continues to speak about the circumstances surrounding his departure from the league.

“I’ve gotten so many questions about why did I protest, what happened, what led up to it, the details behind the scenes of all of the moments,” Kaepernick told TIME while discussing his memoir.

A decade after his protest began, Kaepernick is still pressing the same questions, and Jones remains one of the most recognizable figures connected to the NFL’s response.

articles.title: Emmitt Smith's daughter suggests to Jerry Jones the three signings the Cowboys need to make it back to the Super Bowl
articles.standfirst: Skylar Smith’s nostalgic plea comes as Jerry Jones weighs more moves to strengthen the Cowboys
articles.summary: Skylar Smith’s nostalgic plea comes as Jerry Jones weighs more moves to strengthen the Cowboys
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys’ dramatic 34-30 comeback against the Houston Texans may have lifted the mood around the franchise, but it hasn’t erased the questions surrounding their Super Bowl ambitions.

At 2-2, Dallas has shown plenty of offensive firepower, but defensive concerns and inconsistent late-game execution remain major talking points.

Amid that uncertainty, Skylar Smith , daughter of Cowboys legend Emmitt Smith , offered a nostalgic message that resonated with fans eager to see the glory days return.

After her father shared a throwback photograph with Troy Aikman and Michael Irvin, she commented, “Bring em back!! We need y’all’s help!!” Her message captured the desire to see the attitude and leadership of Dallas’ championship era return.

Emmitt Smith, Aikman and Irvin formed the core of a Cowboys dynasty that captured three Super Bowl titles.

Smith became the NFL’s all-time leading rusher with 18,355 yards, while Aikman established himself as a Hall of Fame quarterback and Irvin became one of the league’s most dangerous receivers.

Their influence still looms over the franchise decades later.

Three additions could change Dallas’ outlook

If Jerry Jones wants to turn the current roster into a legitimate contender, Dallas’ needs point toward three areas: pass rush, secondary depth and offensive-line reinforcement.

The Cowboys have already addressed the latter two to an extent. Dallas acquired offensive tackle Broderick Jones from Pittsburgh in August, adding experience and flexibility up front.

The team then traded for cornerback Joey Porter Jr. after injuries affected its secondary. Porter arrived with 41 career starts and 31 pass breakups through three seasons.

Still, the pass rush remains an obvious concern. Adding an established edge defender capable of consistently pressuring quarterbacks could give Dallas’ defense another dimension, particularly against elite NFC offenses.

Jones has also made it clear that he isn’t closing the door on further moves. He said the Cowboys are open to deals that could improve the team immediately while also providing value beyond the current season.

“The door is always open to get better. I know that’s almost a cliché. But if the right—I’m never shut down from trying to get something that would really advance the needle,” Jones told 105.3 The Fan in Dallas.

“Especially ones that could do it now and into the future. Again, I said at the start of training camp, I am willing to put some things out there that are for today, lean more for today than three years ago. Well, that’s the future we’re talking about.

“So, I am open. We’re open. We’ve got a trade deadline coming up where you can do some things. We’ll see what happens.”

articles.title: Jerry Jones speaks from the heart after Tony Romo’s CBS exit: ‘He’s just getting started’
articles.standfirst: The Cowboys owner’s emotional message reflects a bond that goes beyond football
articles.summary: The Cowboys owner’s emotional message reflects a bond that goes beyond football
articles.body:
J erry Jones’ words about Tony Romo carry the warmth of someone speaking about a person he loves. Their shared history gives his support a meaning that goes beyond the relationship between an NFL franchise owner and his former quarterback. At a difficult moment for Romo, Jones is offering affection, confidence and a reminder that one painful chapter does not have to define everything that follows.

Jones also brings the perspective of a businessman whose experience extends well beyond the Dallas Cowboys. His business ventures include energy investments, and he is the majority shareholder of natural gas producer Comstock Resources. He sees new possibilities for Romo, even as his departure from CBS leaves his next career move uncertain. In Jones’ view, that next chapter begins with Romo taking care of himself.

Jerry Jones sees room for Tony Romo to rebuild

Speaking on 105.3 The Fan on October 7, in comments shared by The Athletic’s Jon Machota , Jones made the personal connection clear. “Tony is one of the most valued relationships that I have on a personal basis. I love him,” he said.

Jones expressed sadness over how the year had unfolded, explaining that he enjoyed what Romo brought to NFL broadcasts and felt proud of his success as a former Cowboy. Yet his message kept returning to the future: “He’s just getting started. He really is. I say that with all sincerity.”

That support comes after CBS and Romo announced their mutual separation on October 2, ending nine years together. Romo had been placed on indefinite leave following his July 23 arrest in Wisconsin for operating a vehicle while intoxicated.

He entered a no-contest plea to the civil charge on September 1. CBS confirmed that J.J. Watt would continue alongside Jim Nantz and Tracy Wolfson on its lead NFL broadcast team for the remainder of the 2026 season.

Jones acknowledged Romo’s mistakes while reflecting on his own. “I can’t look in my mirror without seeing what can happen when you experience mistakes,” he said. Romo, meanwhile, has publicly linked his struggles with alcohol to chronic pain following football injuries and surgeries.

In his departure statement, he said he would take a break to focus on his health and family before pursuing his next opportunity. For now, rebuilding his personal well-being is the priority he has identified.

What comes after that remains open. Jones announced no job offer or broadcasting opportunity, but his confidence was unmistakable. “I don’t know of anyone, period, that has a better future than Tony Romo,” he said, before adding: “He’s not only got great talent, but he’s a hell of a man.”

For Romo, those words offer something meaningful during an uncertain transition: the assurance that someone who knows him beyond his public career still believes in the person and the possibilities ahead.

articles.summary: Prescott’s former fiancée is turning the page with new career ambitions
articles.body:
Sarah Jane Ramos appears ready to enter a new chapter of her life, one that’s being defined by her own ambitions rather than her past relationship with Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott .

Ramos has recently signaled an interest in real estate, sharing an Instagram Story showing the Law of Agency textbook for a 30-hour course through Champions School of Real Estate.

She wrote that she was “2/6th of the way through,” suggesting she’s already making progress toward a potential new qualification. The move adds another dimension to a career that has already included work in the wine and spirits industry.

She’s also taking on a more visible role in Dallas. Ramos was announced as the host of The Huddle Table, a dinner organized by the National Football Wives Association. The event gives her another opportunity to establish herself professionally and publicly while creating an identity that isn’t centered on her connection to Prescott .

That independence comes after an especially turbulent period. Ramos and Prescott began dating in 2023 and later welcomed two daughters, Margaret Jane Rose and Aurora Rayne.

Prescott proposed in October 2024, and the couple had planned to marry in Lake Como, Italy, in April 2026. However, the wedding was canceled in March, only weeks before the ceremony was scheduled to take place.

Ramos turns the page after a very public split

At first, Ramos ’ representative described the breakup as mutual and said there had been no major argument or dramatic blowup before the decision. The statement also emphasized that the former couple remained committed to raising their daughters together.

Prescott later addressed the situation himself, saying there had been “false narratives” surrounding the breakup. The Cowboys quarterback described it as an unfortunate situation and made clear that his focus was on being there for his children.

The public narrative became more complicated in September when Ramos responded to speculation that she was pregnant. She denied the claims and said she was happier after leaving a situation in which she alleged she had been “cheated on repeatedly.”

“Hi everyone. Not pregnant!! Just very thick, eating again and happier than I’ve been in a long time!,” she commented on Instagram.

“That’s usually what happens when you aren’t getting cheated on repeatedly and finally leave a situation that makes you unhappy. Hard for most of you money-obsessed people to believe, I know.”

Although Prescott wasn’t directly named in the comment, the timing and context led many followers to connect the remarks to their relationship. The allegations haven’t been independently confirmed.

articles.title: Jake Ferguson’s $13,611 fine hinged on a drink the NFL thought it recognized
articles.standfirst: The Cowboys tight end won his appeal after explaining the gesture behind his touchdown celebration
articles.summary: The Cowboys tight end won his appeal after explaining the gesture behind his touchdown celebration
articles.body:
One celebration, two possible drinks and a $13,611 difference. When Jake Ferguson pretended to down a beverage after a touchdown against Washington, the NFL saw a player imitating “shotgunning a beer.” The Cowboys tight end said the gesture represented Gatorade. After he challenged that interpretation and presented evidence of the routine’s history, his fine was overturned, ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported on October 7.

The misunderstanding reveals how much meaning people can attach to a simple gesture. Beer became the explanation behind the punishment, although a sports drink was another possibility and the one Ferguson said he intended. He pointed to previous occasions when he had performed the celebration at practice, documented by the Cowboys on social media.

The same gesture tells a different story with context

That history gave Ferguson a way to explain what a brief end-zone moment could not show on its own. His defense placed the celebration within a familiar routine rather than the alcohol reference the NFL had perceived.

The fine was rescinded through the appeals process, although the available reporting does not establish how much weight each piece of evidence carried in the final decision.

There is a human element to the dispute: a gesture can feel obvious to the person making it and mean something entirely different to someone watching. Ferguson’s case illustrates that narrow gap between intention and interpretation.

Schefter also clarified who resolved the disagreement: an appeals officer jointly appointed by the NFL and NFL Players Association, rather than the league simply withdrawing its own assessment. The NFL’s published procedure gives that officer the responsibility to hear both sides.

Ferguson had company in that gap. San Francisco fullback Kyle Juszczyk also successfully challenged a $14,926 fine after explaining that his drinking gesture represented a juice box, a nod to his nickname, “Juice.”

In both cases, a celebration interpreted as drinking beer had another explanation rooted in the player’s own routine or identity. Those explanations emerged when the players had an opportunity to provide context.

articles.summary: Cowboys vs. Buccaneers: Dallas looks to climb at AT&T Stadium against a Tampa Bay team that has yet to win in 2026
articles.body:
The NFL Week 5 begins in Arlington, Texas, and brings a matchup with opposing scripts at AT&T Stadium : the Dallas Cowboys , coming off a late rally in Houston, host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , who are dragging through a forgettable start. Two franchises with a recent playoff past, now separated by an abyss on the scoreboard and in spirit.

What time and where to watch Thursday night's Buccaneers vs Cowboys game

Thursday Night Football can be followed on Prime Video, with NFL+, and to watch the game between Tampa Bay and Dallas, you can do so on KDFW-TV FOX 4. As for the game time, it will start:

Pregame overview of the Buccaneers vs Cowboys

The photo in the overall standings tells a good part of the story. Dallas comes in with a record of 2 wins and 2 losses , sitting in 19th place in the overall standings and third in the East of the National Conference, behind the New York Giants and the Philadelphia Eagles.

The Cowboys are also one of the most productive offenses at the start: they have scored 122 points, a figure that places them among the highest-scoring teams in the entire league. The problem is on the other side of the ball, where they have already allowed 112 points.

Tampa Bay, on the other hand, is going through a bleak start: 0 wins and 4 losses , last place in the NFC South and third from last in the overall standings (29th position).

The Buccaneers have scored just 76 points and have allowed 96, a -20 differential that reflects a stalled offense and a defense that has struggled to close out games.

The Cowboys have alternated between highs and lows. After falling in the opener against the Giants, they responded strongly at home against Washington, let a high-voltage matchup against Baltimore slip away, and pulled it out at the buzzer in Week 4 against Houston. They are a team capable of putting up points in bunches, but they still have not found the consistency to protect leads.

Tampa Bay, meanwhile, has not been able to celebrate. Since the start of the season, they have strung together four losses: to Cincinnati, against Cleveland, versus Minnesota, and, even more painfully, at home to Green Bay by a razor-thin 14-17 in Week 4. The pattern is clear: close games that slip away in the decisive moments. In three of their four losses, the Bucs finished within a touchdown or less.

What's at stake for the Playoffs

Although neither of the two is fighting for the top of its conference today, the context in the NFC East is tight. Dallas is just one win behind the division-leading Giants , so every victory matters in order not to fall out of the playoff conversation.

In a conference where San Francisco and Minnesota remain unbeaten, the Cowboys cannot afford to give up ground against a theoretically inferior opponent. Winning at home is, for Dallas, a positioning obligation.

At the other end, Tampa Bay shares the bottom of the standings with heavyweight names : the Buccaneers join the Los Angeles Chargers, Tennessee, Houston, and Miami in the group of teams still without a win.

For a franchise with ambitions and a roster that reached the postseason last season, falling to 0-5 would be a massive warning sign. The margin for error is now virtually nonexistent: another stumble would leave their playoff hopes in nearly irretrievable territory before reaching the midpoint of the schedule.

What is the forecast for the Buccaneers vs Cowboys?

Everything points to a high-scoring game. Dallas combines home-field advantage, one of the most prolific offenses in the league, and the urgency of not falling behind in its division. Tampa Bay has talent, but its results crisis and the difficulty of closing out games weigh too heavily.

The forecast leans toward a Cowboys victory , although with a porous Texas defense, it would not be surprising if the Buccaneers keep the score alive until the final quarter. If Dallas protects the ball, it should prevail in Arlington.

articles.summary: A cryptic Instagram Story has fans wondering whether Ramos just sent another message to Prescott’s family
articles.body:
Dak Prescott’s former fiancée, Sarah Jane Ramos , appears to have taken another pointed shot at the Dallas Cowboys quarterback’s family, adding to the public fallout following their breakup.

Prescott and Ramos ended their engagement in March 2026, just weeks before they were scheduled to get married in Italy. The former couple, who began dating in 2023, share two daughters, Margaret Jane Rose and Aurora Rayne.

While the split was initially described as mutual, the situation has become increasingly complicated in the months since. Ramos has made comments on social media that appeared to accuse Prescott of repeatedly cheating during their relationship.

Those claims haven’t been independently confirmed, while Prescott has said there have been “false narratives” surrounding the breakup.

Now, Ramos has seemingly directed some of that frustration toward someone in Prescott’s family.

Ramos recently shared an old photograph from a Cowboys game on her Instagram Story. The image showed people sitting in a suite, including an individual wearing a Prescott jersey.

Ramos placed a devil-face emoji over the person’s face, apparently suggesting that the individual was someone from Prescott’s family.

She didn’t identify the person or provide an explanation for the post, leaving followers to speculate about exactly whom she was referring to and why.

The breakup keeps making headlines

The latest social-media post comes after months of attention surrounding the former couple’s relationship. Prescott proposed to Ramos in October 2024, and their wedding was expected to take place in Italy before plans suddenly changed earlier this year.

At the time, Ramos ’ representative characterized the decision as mutual and said there hadn’t been a major fight or dramatic confrontation immediately before the breakup.

That narrative shifted after Ramos responded to online speculation about whether she was pregnant. In an Instagram comment, she denied the pregnancy rumors and appeared to reference infidelity, saying she was happier after leaving a situation in which she had allegedly been repeatedly cheated on.

Prescott has taken a noticeably different approach when discussing the breakup.

“I’ve got too many blessings to look at my trials,” said Prescott . “And I’m just super thankful to that opportunity that I have to be where I am and to have two amazing daughters, to be able to play the quarterback position for this organization and still inspire so many.

“Adversity is going to come. It’s inevitable. And if you know how to respond to it, you can respond to it consistently, you can get over it.”

He’s also indicated that his priority is being present for the couple’s two daughters rather than becoming consumed by the public speculation.

A source close to Ramos previously told People that she wasn’t trying to launch an attack against Prescott with her social-media comments. Instead, the source said she was standing up for herself after remaining quiet while various stories circulated about the breakup.

The source also said Ramos still has considerable affection for Prescott and that the pair remain focused on co-parenting.

Away from the controversy, Ramos is beginning a new professional chapter. She recently shared that she was taking a 30-hour Law of Agency course through Champions School of Real Estate, signaling a possible move into the real-estate industry.

articles.title: Jerry Jones' unexpected support for his former QB Tony Romo after being let go by CBS
articles.standfirst: Cowboys owner sees bright future for Tony Romo despite CBS exit
articles.summary: Cowboys owner sees bright future for Tony Romo despite CBS exit
articles.body:
Tony Romo’s broadcasting career has taken an unexpected turn, but his former boss in Dallas isn’t writing him off.

Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones has publicly backed Romo following the former quarterback’s departure from CBS Sports, offering an optimistic outlook despite the difficult circumstances surrounding the end of his nine-year run with the network.

During his regular appearance on 105.3 The Fan, Jones spoke highly of his former quarterback and made it clear that he believes Romo still has plenty ahead of him.

“He’s just getting started. He really is,” said Jones . “I say that with all sincerity. He’s just getting started. And he certainly has had some — made some mistakes… But he realizes that there’s an area of his life that he wants to do better in.

“He’s got great opportunity ahead of him. I don’t know of anyone — period — that has a better future than Tony Romo. And I’m excited for him. He’s not only got great talent but he’s a hell of a man.”

That backing comes after a turbulent period for Romo . He was arrested in Wisconsin in July on suspicion of operating a vehicle while intoxicated and was subsequently placed on leave by CBS.

The network and Romo eventually announced that they had mutually agreed to part ways, bringing his lengthy broadcasting tenure to an end.

Romo’s next chapter could still be in broadcasting

Romo joined CBS in 2017 after walking away from the NFL and quickly became one of the most recognizable voices in football broadcasting.

His partnership with play-by-play announcer Jim Nantz became a major part of CBS’s NFL coverage, with the pair regularly handling some of the network’s biggest games.

CBS showed just how highly it valued Romo in 2020 when he signed a reported 10-year, $180 million contract. The agreement made him one of the highest-paid sports broadcasters in the industry and demonstrated the network’s confidence in his ability to remain a major part of its NFL coverage.

That chapter is now over. J.J. Watt has stepped into the lead analyst role alongside Nantz and Tracy Wolfson for the remainder of the 2026 season. Watt had previously worked on CBS’s second broadcast team before being elevated following Romo’s departure.

Watt’s promotion also gives CBS a chance to evaluate its new lead booth. The former Houston Texans star has already received plenty of attention for his transition from the playing field to broadcasting, and his performance could influence the network’s plans for the 2027 season.

articles.title: CeeDee Lamb injury update: What happened to the Cowboys’ star wide receiver?
articles.standfirst: CeeDee Lamb left the Cowboys’ Week 5 matchup against the Buccaneers.
articles.summary: CeeDee Lamb left the Cowboys’ Week 5 matchup against the Buccaneers.
articles.body:
CeeDee Lamb was on the verge of making history with the Dallas Cowboys ahead of their Week 5 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . The wide receiver was coming off a performance in which he recorded 189 yards and a touchdown on 17 receptions against the Houston Texans , and he was close to becoming just the third player in franchise history to record 500 yards and five touchdowns in the first five games of a season.

However, it appears he will fall short. Lamb had a quiet night against Tampa Bay, recording just two receptions for nine yards before leaving the game with a quadriceps injury.

With Dallas trailing 24-10 , the offense took the field without him, and it was later reported that his return was questionable.

Lamb watched from the sideline as the Cowboys marched 99 yards down the field , capping the drive with a 17-yard touchdown pass to George Pickens to cut the deficit to 24-16 . Dallas attempted a two-point conversion but failed, a play that summed up its difficult night.

Cowboys dealing with more injuries beyond CeeDee Lamb

Injuries have been a constant theme for Dallas throughout the season, and the team suffered a setback just before kickoff : cornerback Joey Porter Jr. , acquired in a trade last week, was ruled out due to an illness.

Other players also dealt with physical issues during the game. Safety Alijah Clark is dealing with a hamstring injury, and his return is questionable.

Pickens was also banged up during the 99-yard drive and went to the sideline to have his shoulder examined.

On the following defensive series, rookie linebacker Jaishawn Barham took a hit and briefly left the field to be evaluated. Additionally, starting left tackle Tyler Guyton , who has had a dominant season, was also ruled out with a back injury, with Broderick Jones stepping in to replace him.

Dallas gets one of its key players back for Week 5

The Cowboys received some good news before the game with the return of Tyler Smith . The All-Pro left guard underwent thumb surgery before Week 1 and missed the first four games of the season.

Smith returned to the starting lineup and performed well on the opening offensive drive, opening up running lanes for Javonte Williams . However, after that possession, Dallas had to rely on the passing game because the Buccaneers managed to shut down the ground attack.

articles.title: Jerry Jones drops brutal two-word statement after Cowboys’ loss to Buccaneers
articles.standfirst: Jerry Jones didn’t hold back after the Cowboys’ disappointing loss to the Buccaneers.
articles.summary: Jerry Jones didn’t hold back after the Cowboys’ disappointing loss to the Buccaneers.
articles.body:
Jerry Jones made no secret of his disappointment after the Dallas Cowboys suffered a 24-16 home loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , a result that raises concerns and exposes the doubts surrounding the team.

The Dallas owner, who enjoyed tremendous success in the 1990s when the franchise won three Super Bowl titles , is now facing a very different reality. The Cowboys missed the playoffs in each of the last two seasons , and although they entered this campaign with renewed expectations, they have yet to establish themselves as legitimate contenders.

Dallas boasts an explosive offense and made adjustments to strengthen its defense, but the loss to Tampa Bay leaves the team with a 2-3 record. The result is even more concerning because the Buccaneers played without their starting quarterback, Baker Mayfield , who is injured.

From his usual suite, Jones watched as his team's mistakes at crucial moments sealed the outcome. After the game, the Cowboys owner was asked about the team's performance and summed up his feelings with a blunt statement.

“Extraordinarily disappointing,” Jones said after the game.

The Cowboys expose their weaknesses against Tampa Bay

The loss once again put Dallas' performance on both sides of the ball under scrutiny. The team showed some positive signs in the first half but lost control after halftime and failed to respond to Tampa Bay's surge.

The Cowboys went into the locker room with a 10-7 lead, but the Buccaneers answered with 17 points in the third quarter to change the course of the game. Dallas attempted a late comeback, but its hopes ended when the opposing defense intercepted Dak Prescott's final pass of the night.

The quarterback struggled to deliver in key moments, completing 24 of 42 passes for 316 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions.

In the running game, Javonte Williams led the way with 12 carries for 45 yards and a touchdown . Meanwhile, George Pickens delivered his best performance of the season, recording nine receptions for 130 yards and a touchdown.

Green Bay, Dallas' next test

The Cowboys will have little time to dwell on the loss. Their next game will be on the road against the Green Bay Packers in Week 6 , a matchup that will test their ability to bounce back after a defeat that left Jones bitterly disappointed.

articles.title: Dak Prescott's powerful message to the employee who felt ashamed of the Cowboys: "Don't coward away"
articles.standfirst: The Dallas quarterback challenged a stadium worker to stand behind his criticism after the Cowboys suffered a frustrating 24-16 defeat to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers
articles.summary: The Dallas quarterback challenged a stadium worker to stand behind his criticism after the Cowboys suffered a frustrating 24-16 defeat to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers
articles.body:
D ak Prescott had a message for the person who called the Dallas Cowboys “embarrassing” after their latest defeat: if you are willing to criticize someone, have the courage to say it to their face.

The Cowboys quarterback became involved in a tense exchange with a worker in the stadium’s postgame area on Thursday, October 8, after Dallas lost 24-16 to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at AT&T Stadium.

The defeat was particularly disappointing because Tampa Bay had entered the game without a win during the 2026 season, while Dallas was playing at home under the national spotlight of Thursday Night Football.

The result left the Cowboys with a 2-3 record and gave the Buccaneers their first victory of the campaign.

According to local FOX station KDFW, a stadium worker said “embarrassing” as Prescott walked past on his way back to the locker room.

Reporter Sam Gannon later clarified that the individual was a “car service driver.” Video of the interaction subsequently circulated online, capturing the comment and Prescott’s response.

In another clip, Prescott appeared to call the individual a “tough guy” before demanding that he be removed from the area.

"Get his (expletive) out of here," the quarterback said.

The exchange quickly became a talking point after a game that had already left Dallas searching for answers.

Prescott was asked about the confrontation during his postgame media availability, where he made clear that he was not necessarily objecting to the worker expressing an opinion about the team.

"I mean, not that they're wrong," Prescott began, adding "but the thing was you know, I just ... I don't know if it was an employee, if it was a driver, whoever it was, he's free to speak his mind."

However, Prescott took issue with the way the criticism was delivered, suggesting that the person appeared unwilling to stand behind the remark once the quarterback turned to face him.

"You know when he said it, I just happened to look at him and at that point he looked away, didn't look, and then when I turned my head back he said something else," Prescott said. "That's the part just, as a man or as a person, feel free to speak your mind. Just speak it. Don't coward away from the reaction that you're going to get.

"If you're saying it's embarrassing, say it's embarrassing, if you're saying it to me then say it to me. You know what I mean? ... Hate it that it's even being talked about to be honest with you."

Prescott explains why he stopped short of calling the defeat embarrassing

While the confrontation generated attention, the circumstances behind it were difficult for Dallas to ignore.

The Cowboys had entered the matchup with an opportunity to improve their record against a team that had yet to win a game, but they struggled to contain Tampa Bay and repeatedly gave the visitors chances to take control.

Prescott finished with 316 passing yards and a touchdown on 24 completions from 42 attempts, but two interceptions proved costly.

The second came late in the fourth quarter, when a pass intended for tight end Jake Ferguson was deflected into the air and intercepted by Tampa Bay linebacker Alex Anzalone . That turnover effectively ended Dallas’ hopes of completing a comeback.

The quarterback nevertheless resisted describing the entire performance as embarrassing, explaining that doing so could take credit away from Tampa Bay’s efforts.

"To use the word embarrassing is tough. I feel like I'm discrediting the NFL if I use that and particularly the Tampa Bay Bucs and a great Todd Bowles, defensive coached team. ... The plan and what (the Bucs) did tonight is the reason for (this loss). To say embarrassing I think I'd be discrediting them, but we were definitely supposed to win this game,” he said.

"This is a game that we were supposed to have on paper or whichever way you want to look at it. I think ( Brian Schottenheimer ) said it best in the locker room, in this league you got to win the games you're supposed to win. When a winless team comes into your home stadium on a Thursday night, prime-time game, yeah, we're supposed to win that. So, it sucks and right up there close to embarrassing but I don't know if I would say that."

Prescott’s comments reflected the tension between acknowledging Dallas’ disappointing performance and recognizing that the Buccaneers deserved credit.

Tampa Bay produced 419 total yards, compared with Dallas’ 366, and controlled possession for more than 39 minutes. Running back Bucky Irving rushed for 165 yards, including a 72-yard run that helped set up Tampa Bay’s go-ahead touchdown early in the second half.

The Cowboys , meanwhile, managed only 50 rushing yards as a team and committed three turnovers. Those numbers left Dallas with plenty to address beyond the postgame confrontation.

Head coach Brian Schottenheimer was also asked about the incident. Rather than rejecting the worker’s right to voice an opinion, he described the criticism as something that could motivate the team.

"We believe in what we're doing," the second-year head coach continued. "We believe that we have good players, good coaches. We believe the solution is in this room. We're going to get back to work."

When a reporter asked whether he considered the comment disrespectful, Schottenheimer pushed back against the wording of the question.

"I didn't say I didn't take it as disrespect. You said that," Schottenheimer shot back. "I didn't say that. I said it's motivating. People are allowed to say what they want to say."

The coach’s response echoed Prescott’s acknowledgment that people are entitled to their opinions, even if the quarterback clearly disliked the manner in which this particular criticism was delivered.

For Dallas, the more pressing issue is what happens next. A 2-3 record puts pressure on the Cowboys to respond, particularly after losing to a previously winless opponent in front of their home crowd.

Prescott’s statistics showed that he was able to move the ball through the air, but the turnovers and struggles on the ground undermined the offense’s chances.

His message to the worker was ultimately about accountability: criticism is fair game, but he believes people should be prepared to stand behind what they say.

The Cowboys will now need to demonstrate that same willingness to take responsibility on the field as they attempt to recover from a defeat that left players, coaches and supporters frustrated.
