articles.title: Jerry Jones doesn't stop his fury: he slams his hand on the table while George Pickens tries to destroy his helmet
articles.standfirst: The Cowboys owner and wide receiver could barely hide their frustration after Dak Prescott’s late interception helped seal a painful 24-16 defeat
articles.summary: The Cowboys owner and wide receiver could barely hide their frustration after Dak Prescott’s late interception helped seal a painful 24-16 defeat
articles.body:
J erry Jones and George Pickens offered two very different views of the same frustration as the Dallas Cowboys watched their hopes of a comeback disappear against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Thursday night.

Dallas entered the October 8 matchup looking to build on its recent victory and move above .500. Instead, the Cowboys suffered a damaging 24-16 home defeat against a Tampa Bay team that had yet to win a game during the 2026 season.

The result dropped Dallas to 2-3, while the Buccaneers finally got their first victory of the campaign.

The most painful moment arrived in the closing stages, when the Cowboys still had an opportunity to make the score level. With Dallas trailing by eight points and less than 90 seconds remaining, quarterback Dak Prescott attempted to find tight end Jake Ferguson over the middle.

The pass struck Ferguson’s hands before bouncing into the air, allowing Tampa Bay linebacker Alex Anzalone to collect the interception. The turnover extinguished Dallas’ comeback hopes and provided the Buccaneers with possession at a crucial moment.

The reaction inside AT&T Stadium was immediate. Jones, watching from his suite, was seen slamming his hand down in frustration. On the sideline, Pickens responded by throwing his helmet forcefully onto the turf, visibly furious at how the game had unfolded.

The contrasting reactions captured the mood surrounding a Cowboys team that had entered the contest with expectations of winning comfortably.

Instead, Dallas left the field with another defeat and fresh questions about its ability to turn promising performances into consistent results.

Pickens had done little to deserve individual blame for the loss. The wide receiver recorded nine receptions for 130 yards and a touchdown, giving Prescott a productive target throughout the contest.

His late touchdown helped Dallas close the gap to 24-16, but the attempted two-point conversion failed, leaving the Cowboys needing another score.

Jones admits the Cowboys missed a major opportunity

The owner did not hide his disappointment when he addressed reporters after the final whistle. Although he acknowledged Tampa Bay’s performance, his comments made clear that he believed Dallas had let an important opportunity slip away.

“I, of course, appreciated any chance we might have had there near the end,” Jones told reporters after the game.

“But the Buccaneers really took it to us. In my view, they did it inside. That’s where the real damage was done, we’ll see. That’s really surprising to me. That’s what it is, we missed a great opportunity to build something here, but they really all the way, probably most all the phases, they won it tonight. … This is very disappointing, and I know it’s disappointing to our home crowd, it is to me.”

Jones ’ assessment pointed toward a broader problem than one interception. Tampa Bay controlled the game physically, particularly through its rushing attack, and consistently made Dallas work for possession.

The Buccaneers finished with 419 total yards, compared with the Cowboys ’ 366, while holding the ball for more than 39 minutes.

Running back Bucky Irving was central to that advantage. He rushed for a career-high 165 yards and scored twice, including a 72-yard run early in the second half that helped set up the go-ahead touchdown.

His final 22-yard run after Prescott’s interception also helped Tampa Bay close out the victory.

The Buccaneers achieved that result despite being without starting quarterback Baker Mayfield , who was sidelined by a thumb injury. Rookie Jalon Daniels stepped in and completed 19 of 25 passes for 189 yards and a touchdown, avoiding the costly turnovers that hurt Dallas.

Prescott, meanwhile, finished with 316 passing yards and one touchdown, but his two interceptions proved decisive. Both came after passes were tipped by receivers, yet the turnovers still highlighted how little margin Dallas had for error.

The Cowboys also struggled to establish a consistent ground game, managing only 50 rushing yards as a team. That imbalance left Prescott carrying much of the offensive responsibility and made the late turnover even more damaging.

Pickens ’ performance was one of the few bright spots for Dallas. His 130 receiving yards and touchdown demonstrated the threat he can provide, but the result meant his contribution ultimately went unrewarded.

The wider concern for Jones and the Cowboys is whether the team can address the weaknesses exposed by Tampa Bay. Losing to a previously winless opponent at home is a setback, particularly for a team that had hoped to build momentum after its previous victory.

Jones ’ visible anger and Pickens ’ sideline outburst reflected the disappointment of a night that Dallas had every reason to approach with confidence. But the Buccaneers earned their win by controlling the line of scrimmage, producing explosive plays and taking advantage of Dallas’ mistakes.

For the Cowboys , the challenge now is to turn that frustration into a response. Prescott’s final interception provided the defining image of the defeat, but the problems that led to it had been building throughout the game.

Unless Dallas can improve its ball security, running game and defensive consistency, Jones may have more reasons to show his displeasure in the weeks ahead.

articles.title: Joey Porter Jr.'s worrying illness that prevented him from playing with the Cowboys: "His condition worsened"
articles.standfirst: The Dallas cornerback was ruled out shortly before kickoff against Tampa Bay after arriving at AT&T Stadium feeling seriously unwell
articles.summary: The Dallas cornerback was ruled out shortly before kickoff against Tampa Bay after arriving at AT&T Stadium feeling seriously unwell
articles.body:
Joey Porter Jr. ’s anticipated home debut with the Dallas Cowboys ended before it could begin after the cornerback was ruled inactive for Thursday night’s game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers because of a sudden illness.

The late change came as a surprise because Porter had been expected to build on his first appearance for Dallas, having recently joined the team in a trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers .

Instead, reports indicated that the 26-year-old was too unwell to participate after arriving at AT&T Stadium.

According to NFL insider Jane Slater , a Cowboys source described Porter as "very sick" when he reached the team facility, prompting the organisation to send him home. NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo subsequently reported that Porter was "vomiting with a bad virus."

The Cowboys did not publicly provide a more detailed medical diagnosis, meaning the precise nature of the illness remained unclear.

Nevertheless, the reported symptoms were severe enough to prevent the defensive back from playing in a game that Dallas had hoped would provide another opportunity to strengthen its struggling defence.

Porter’s absence was particularly frustrating given how recently he had arrived in Texas. Dallas acquired him from Pittsburgh on September 30, sending the Steelers a 2027 sixth-round draft pick and a 2028 second-round selection.

The move was intended to improve a secondary that had already faced personnel difficulties during the opening weeks of the season.

He made his Cowboys debut against the Houston Texans on October 4, recording 25 defensive snaps in a 34-30 victory. Porter had been eased into the lineup, with the expectation that his workload could increase as he became more familiar with the defensive system.

Thursday’s matchup against Tampa Bay appeared to offer another step in that process. However, the unexpected illness meant Dallas had to reconsider its defensive arrangements shortly before the game began.

Why Porter’s absence created another problem for Dallas

Porter’s arrival was significant because the Cowboys had been looking for solutions in their secondary.

Before the trade, the cornerback had missed Pittsburgh’s first three regular-season games after spending training camp sidelined by a reported back issue. His absence had also been linked to a contract dispute, making his eventual move to Dallas a notable development in his season.

The Cowboys were therefore hoping that a fresh start would allow Porter to establish himself as a regular contributor. His debut against Houston offered an initial opportunity, but the illness interrupted his progress just as the team was considering giving him more responsibility.

Dallas also had other defensive concerns entering Thursday’s contest. Cornerback Cobie Durant was unavailable because of a hamstring problem, while linebacker DeMarvion Overshown was sidelined with a hamstring injury.

Those absences made the sudden loss of another defensive back more difficult to manage.

DaRon Bland was among the players expected to take on additional responsibilities in the secondary, while Ameer Speed and other defensive backs could be asked to contribute more snaps.

Such adjustments can be particularly challenging when they are made close to kickoff, leaving coaches little time to prepare alternative combinations.

The timing also mattered because Tampa Bay was starting rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels in place of the injured Baker Mayfield .

Dallas would have wanted its defensive backs ready to handle the Buccaneers’ passing attack, particularly with Daniels making another start while adjusting to the NFL.

Ultimately, the Cowboys lost 24-16, as Tampa Bay secured its first victory of the season. The defeat left Dallas with a 2-3 record and added pressure on a defence that had already struggled to deliver consistent performances.

Porter’s absence should not automatically be interpreted as a long-term setback. The available reports described an acute illness, but Dallas had not announced a detailed diagnosis or a projected recovery timetable.

His availability for the team’s next game would depend on how quickly he recovered and whether he was ready to return to full participation.

For now, the priority will be his recovery. After missing the start of the season in Pittsburgh and making only one appearance for Dallas before Thursday, Porter will hope to return soon and begin making the impact the Cowboys expected when they completed the trade.

articles.title: Jerry Jones receives an ultimatum and a proposal with the perfect coach to replace Brian Schottenheimer
articles.standfirst: The Cowboys' latest loss has left everyone very upset with the team's performance
articles.summary: The Cowboys' latest loss has left everyone very upset with the team's performance
articles.body:
The Cowboys once again dashed Dallas fans' hopes in another forgettable home game against the Buccaneers . The 16-24 loss has hurt so much that many are already calling on Jerry Jones to immediately bring an end to the era of Brian Schottenheimer as head coach.

It is true that we are only in Week 5 and that there is still a lot of season left to play, but the Cowboys are already below .500 with a 2-3 record and they are losing games that could later keep them out of the playoffs. Which would be another catastrophe for the Jones family.

One of the harshest critics after the latest disaster was former Steelers player Breiden Fehoko , who gave Jerry Jones an ultimatum to take drastic measures in the coming hours. He even gave him the name of the coach who could solve the Cowboys' problems to make things easier for him.

Why Mike Tomlin is the perfect coach for the Cowboys

' Schottenheimer has to be fired. Mike Tomlin needs to be in Dallas tomorrow for the head coaching job . This is serious," he explained. And for Fehoko, the one to blame for the current situation is not Dak Prescott , as some point out: "The defense can't stop even a nosebleed . This is not Dak Prescott's fault. I'm not going to blame him. He is the best quarterback in the NFC". '

The defense can't stop even a nosebleed. This is not Dak Prescott's fault

Mike Tomlin is without a team after leaving the Steelers in a decision that surprised many after 19 seasons with the franchise. Meanwhile, Brian Schottenheimer is not convincing anyone at the helm of Dallas, especially after last year in his first stint ended with a 7-9-1 record that amounted to another major disappointment.

Now the final say will, as always, belong to Jerry Jones, although it seems unlikely that he will make any rash decision. However, his words after the defeat and his visible anger during the game leave open the possibility that he may do what he usually does: “Extraordinarily disappointing ,” said the owner before leaving AT&T Stadium.

articles.title: Another mistake by Tony Romo condemns him to a disastrous end, while Jerry Jones could make changes to the Cowboys
articles.standfirst: The former Dallas quarterback endured a difficult day after losing his CBS broadcasting role and being disqualified from a golf qualifier
articles.summary: The former Dallas quarterback endured a difficult day after losing his CBS broadcasting role and being disqualified from a golf qualifier
articles.body:
T ony Romo suffered two major setbacks on October 2, when CBS Sports confirmed that it had parted ways with the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback and he was subsequently disqualified from a golf tournament after submitting an incorrect scorecard.

The double disappointment marked a difficult moment for Romo , who had spent nine seasons as CBS’ lead NFL game analyst after retiring from professional football.

His broadcasting future is now uncertain, while his latest attempt to advance through golf’s qualifying system ended in controversy over a scoring error.

Romo was competing in the final round of a Korn Ferry Tour pre-qualifier in Oklahoma, hoping to progress towards the developmental tour. However, his scorecard recorded a four on both the 16th and 17th holes when the scores should have been five on each.

According to reports from Yahoo Sports and ProFootballTalk, Romo accepted responsibility for the mistake. His group had reportedly been placed on the clock because of slow play, potentially contributing to the rushed situation.

Under golf’s rules, signing for a score lower than the one actually achieved results in disqualification.

Even if the scorecard had been correct, Romo was not expected to advance to the next stage. Nevertheless, the incident added another setback to a day already dominated by the end of his broadcasting career.

Romo’s broadcasting future remains uncertain as the Cowboys face their own problems

CBS announced its separation from Romo after he had been placed on indefinite leave following his July arrest in Wisconsin for operating a vehicle while intoxicated. He pleaded no contest to the charge in September, according to the Associated Press.

The network said: "CBS Sports and Tony Romo have mutually agreed to part ways. We thank Tony for his contributions over the past nine years and wish him the best moving forward."

Former Houston Texans defensive end J.J. Watt , who had filled in during Romo’s absence, will remain alongside play-by-play announcer Jim Nantz and reporter Tracy Wolfson on CBS’ lead NFL broadcast team. The change leaves Romo without his prominent weekly role as the network’s top game analyst.

Romo initially earned widespread praise after moving into broadcasting in 2017, particularly for his ability to anticipate plays before they unfolded. His detailed knowledge of offensive schemes helped distinguish him from many other former players who transitioned into television.

However, the end of his CBS tenure creates questions about what comes next. Romo has indicated that his immediate priorities are his health and family, leaving any potential return to broadcasting or other professional opportunities unresolved.

Meanwhile, the Cowboys are dealing with a different kind of pressure. Jerry Jones , the franchise’s owner and general manager, has already indicated that Dallas is willing to explore roster additions if the right opportunities arise.

The team had been looking for reinforcements following injuries in its secondary and an inconsistent start to the season.

Dallas’ 24-16 defeat to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on October 8 intensified scrutiny of the team. The Cowboys fell to 2-3, while Tampa Bay secured its first win of the campaign.

The result raised further questions about Dallas’ defensive performance and its ability to turn individual talent into consistent results.

Jones could therefore consider personnel changes or further trades as the season develops, although there is no confirmation that a major overhaul is imminent. The owner has previously expressed a willingness to pursue upgrades, particularly where injuries have exposed weaknesses.

Romo’s golf disqualification and CBS departure are not directly connected to decisions about the Cowboys’ roster.

Yet both stories illustrate how quickly circumstances can change in professional sport. For Romo , the immediate task is deciding what comes after broadcasting, while Jones must determine how to give Dallas a better chance of competing.

Romo may still pursue golf, but his latest qualifying attempt ended before he could make progress. For the Cowboys, the next challenge is to respond on the field before their season slips further off course.

articles.title: Connor Wood joins the Cowboys cheerleaders, but his path to the spotlight began with losing a job
articles.standfirst: The comedian known as Fibula brings his playful energy to the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders
articles.summary: The comedian known as Fibula brings his playful energy to the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders
articles.body:
Connor Wood has pom-poms in his hands and a routine to follow. For viewers discovering him alongside the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders, he might look like an influencer enjoying an unexpected dance opportunity. For longtime followers, the scene feels familiar: Connor stepping into a new situation and taking everyone along for the experience.

“Can’t take the Texas out of Connor.” Wood was born in Austin, and the reference to his roots accompanies a collaboration the cheerleaders described as a detour from the Dancing with the Stars ballroom to the field. He is currently competing on the show with professional dancer Rylee Arnold.

Before the pom-poms, Connor Wood had to start over

His entertainment career began in a much less glamorous setting. After working in marketing for companies including Bumble and Bird, Wood lost his job during the pandemic. In interviews, he has described posting videos about looking for work, unsuccessful job interviews and the uncertainty surrounding that chapter of his life. People recognized their own experiences in his stories, giving his humor an audience.

Under the name Fibula, he turned those everyday observations into a following and eventually a career. Today, his work spans social media, stand-up comedy and Brooke and Connor Make a Podcast , which he co-hosts with Brooke Averick. His official ABC biography credits him with more than 1.5 million followers across platforms and notes that Adweek named their show its Best Comedy Podcast of 2024.

That success also created a moment his family could share. Wood told PEOPLE that when he returned for a hometown performance, his mother gathered around 30 friends, arranged a party bus and bought tables in the front row. Behind the growing audience was a family showing up to celebrate a career that had taken an unexpected turn.

Now, dancing is introducing him to another audience. His appearance on Dancing with the Stars provides context for the Cowboys cheerleaders collaboration: a comedian accustomed to telling stories is learning to communicate through movement. The squad’s official posts document their time together, although they do not explain who arranged the visit or how the invitation came about.

articles.title: Brian Schottenheimer is worried: Jerry Jones could take action and fire his coach after another Cowboys disaster
articles.standfirst: The 24-16 defeat to the previously winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers is a disappointing blow.
articles.summary: The 24-16 defeat to the previously winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers is a disappointing blow.
articles.body:
Brian Schottenheimer is facing mounting pressure after the Dallas Cowboys suffered a damaging loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Thursday night after hosts entered the game as a strong favorite, but instead fell 24-16 at the AT&T Stadium . The loss came against a team that had lost its first four games of the season and was starting rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels and dropped the Cowboys to 2-3, whilst Tampa Bay recorded its first victory of the campaign.

For Schottenheimer , the result was particularly concerning because Dallas had just beaten the Houston Texans and appeared to be building momentum and now, questions are being asked about whether Jerry Jones will consider changes if the team continues to underperform. Schottenheimer is in his second season as Dallas ’ head coach after taking over in 2025 and his first campaign already exposed defensive weaknesses, and the early signs in the new season suggest those problems have not been resolved as the NFC East team entered Thursday’s contest allowing 389.5 yards and 28 points per game. The defense is among the league’s poorest statistically and the performance against Tampa Bay did little to ease those concerns as Daniels completed 19 of 25 passes for 189 yards and a touchdown. Bucky Irving produced a career-best 165 rushing yards and scored twice as the Buccaneers finished with 419 total yards, repeatedly exploiting Dallas ’ inability to stop the run and contain explosive plays.

Costly mistakes leave Schottenheimer under growing pressure

Tampa Bay initially trailed 10-7 at halftime, but the game changed dramatically after Irving broke free for a 72-yard run early in the third quarter. The play set up a touchdown for Emeka Egbuka , giving the Buccaneers the lead and shifting momentum away from the home team. Dallas then struggled to regain control. Prescott threw two interceptions, while a kickoff fumble by KaVontae Turpin handed Tampa Bay another opportunity. The Buccaneers capitalized, extending their advantage and forcing the Cowboys into a desperate chase. There was a brief chance for a comeback when George Pickens caught a 17-yard touchdown pass following a 99-yard drive, however, the two-point conversion failed, leaving the Cowboys needing another score. After Tampa Bay went three-and-out, Prescott had an opportunity to lead a late tying drive, but a pass intended for tight end Jake Ferguson deflected off his hands and was intercepted by linebacker Alex Anzalone . The turnover effectively ended Dallas ’ hopes as Prescott finished with 316 passing yards and a touchdown, but, once again, interceptions proved costly. Schottenheimer cannot be blamed for every individual mistake, but the broader defensive issues fall under his responsibility as head coach.

Dallas has struggled to prevent opponents from sustaining drives, and the latest defeat exposed how quickly the team can lose control when turnovers begin to pile up and for a man like Jones , who has long demanded results from a franchise that expects to compete for Super Bowls , he could be tempted to make a switch. However, neither the Cowboys nor Jones , their owner and general manager, has not announced any decision about Schottenheimer 's job – but another defeat of this nature is unlikely to strengthen the coach’s position. There is, however, a distinction between mounting pressure and an imminent dismissal as Dallas still has most of the regular season ahead of them and a stronger run of performances could change the conversation quickly. Especially as the NFC East , as a group continues, to struggle with none of the New York Giants , Philadelphia Eagles or Washington Commanders racing into a clear lead. So, the coming weeks will therefore be important. Dallas must improve its tackling, limit explosive plays and protect the football more consistently. The offence has enough talent to compete, but it cannot continually compensate for defensive breakdowns and turnovers.

articles.title: Jerry Jones's generous gesture toward one of the Cowboys' stars “clashes” with his image as a tough businessman
articles.standfirst: Jones made the gesture of a lifetime to Dallas’ Shemar James
articles.summary: Jones made the gesture of a lifetime to Dallas’ Shemar James
articles.body:
T he Dallas Cowboys owner, Jerry Jones , demonstrated a personal side of his leadership when he helped Shemar James return home to be with his wife as she went into labor, arranging private air travel and transportation to the hospital.

The gesture came after the Cowboys secured a 34-30 victory over the Houston Texans in Week 4, improving their record to 2-2 and temporarily bring their NFL season back to life as Dak Prescott connected with CeeDee Lamb for a 12-yard touchdown with 40 seconds remaining, sealing the win.

Next up for the Cowboys is a meeting against Green Bay on October 18. The Packers will not have Micah Parsons available, and now Dallas may not have Lamb either.

articles.standfirst: The Cheerleaders will link up with an esteemed brand in Charlotte Tilbury
articles.summary: The Cheerleaders will link up with an esteemed brand in Charlotte Tilbury
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders have secured another year of support from Charlotte Tilbury , extending a partnership that brings the beauty brand into the group's game-day preparations. Charlotte Tilbury partners with the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders for a second season, expanding its collaboration through retail appearances, creator experiences, digital content and in-stadium activations.

The venture will also see a new range of products released, covering skin care, which include Magic Cream , Magic Serum Crystal Elixir , Hollywood Skin Secrets Immediate Eye Revival Patches and Invisible UV Flawless Primer SPF 50 . Whilst a new complexion range features Airbrush Flawless Foundation , Airbrush Flawless Blur Concealer , Airbrush Flawless Finish , Airbrush Flawless Blur Loose Powder and Airbrush Flawless Setting Spray . Additional products also include Hollywood Contour Wand , Airbrush Bronzer, Beauty Light Wands , Exagger-Eyes Volume Mascara , and Legendary Brows and Pillow Talk lip products. And the renewal of the partnership is a very positive sign according to the senior director of the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders , and a welcome change from the team's on-field woes. "Looking good makes you feel good and feeling good gives you confidence," said Kelli Finglass . "That's what we love about Charlotte Tilbury. It's a brand that's really about confidence and helping women feel their best. “For the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders, that confidence is so important because when they feel good about themselves, they can step out on the field and perform at their very best."

Schottenheimer reacts to Week 5 loss as NFL Playoffs hopes fade

The Cowboys contend with growing pressure following a disappointing Week 5 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , a defeat that left head coach Brian Schottenheimer frustrated with his team's performance. The Cowboys struggled across all three phases against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , surrendering 241 rushing yards and two touchdowns as Jalon Daniels starred and made plays that compounded Dallas ' difficulties throughout the contest. Schottenheimer acknowledged the shortcomings after the game, describing the defeat as a missed opportunity and emphasizing that his team had failed to meet the standard required to win in the NFL . "Disappointed, for sure," said Schottenheimer . "I told the guys in [the locker room] that it was a missed opportunity. We didn't really play well in all three phases, and certainly not good enough to win a game in the National Football League. And they know that. "Again, it comes down to this being the National Football League, and it's going to come down to the fourth quarter. And even with as poorly as we performed, we had a chance to still get back in and try to win the game, and we came up short." The defeat has raised questions about what needs to change before Dallas faces the Green Bay Packers on October 18, even after acquiring Joey Porter Jr. from the Pittsburgh Steelers .

articles.title: “Bring Mike Tomlin to Dallas Now”: Fans demand Jerry Jones fire Brian Schottenheimer to save Dak Prescott
articles.standfirst: Could the Dallas Cowboys turn to the former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach?
articles.summary: Could the Dallas Cowboys turn to the former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach?
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys are facing renewed calls for a coaching change after their 24-16 defeat to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , with former defensive tackle Breiden Fehoko urging Jerry Jones to replace Brian Schottenheimer with Mike Tomlin . Dallas dropped to 2-3 after shocking losing at AT&T Stadium to a Tampa Bay team that entered the matchup without a win and was missing starting quarterback Baker Mayfield – a team the Cowboys were tipped to demolish.

Undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels led the Buccaneers instead, but the visitors still managed to control possession and capitalize on three Cowboys turnovers and the result intensified scrutiny of Schottenheimer . He will have been in the role for two years come January 2027 but the questions about his leadership have grown as Dallas struggles to turn its offensive production into victories, and the defense continues to struggle. Jerry Jones has dismissed the possibility as of replacing Schottenheimer "premature”, but Fehoko , however, believes the franchise needs a more decisive response if they hope to reach the NFL Playoffs. The 28-year-old, who played in the NFL from 2020-2024, used social media to make his case for the former Pittsburgh head coach to take over in Dallas – and he also defended Dak Prescott . “Dak Prescott went 24/42 for 300-plus yards, one touchdown, and both of his interceptions came off of guys dropping it wide open in their hands,” Fehoko posted on X.com, formerly Twitter. “Tip drill, and both picks go to the defense. “I can’t stress enough how much help Dak Prescott needs. He doesn’t have a defense. Christian Parker, he’s out here with Cartier glasses and baby diamond studs in his ears. Defense can’t stop a nosebleed. “CeeDee Lamb gets hurt; Dak still throws for 300-plus, goes 99 yards when they need him to. Schottenheimer, you got to get fired. Mike Tomlin needs to be in Dallas tomorrow for the head coaching job. “This is bad. This is not on Dak Prescott. Not going for that. He’s the best quarterback in the NFC.”

Prescott hits back at fan who called Cowboys loss embarrassing

Fehoko 's comments reflect the frustration surrounding a team expected to compete, and although Prescott' s two interceptions proved costly, he argued that the circumstances surrounding those plays and the wider defensive shortcomings made it unfair to solely blame primarily on the quarterback. Prescott also addressed an uncomfortable moment involving a stadium worker after Thursday's defeat, criticizing the employee for appearing to withdraw his comments once the quarterback realized what had been said. The worker reportedly described the loss as "embarrassing" whilst Prescott was walking toward the locker room, although the veteran later explained that he took issue not with the criticism itself. He took issue with the apparent change in the worker's behavior after their eyes met, feeling the stadium worker could not commit to his attitude. "When he said it, I just happened to look at him, and at that point, he looked away," Prescott said. "And when I turned my head back, he said something else. “And so that's the part that, just as a man or as just a person, feel free to speak your mind. Just speak it. Don't cower away from the reaction that you're going to get. And so, if you're saying it's embarrassing, say it's embarrassing. “If you're saying it to me, then say it to me. Don't go back on it. So that's all that was, and hate that it's even being talked about, to be honest with you."

articles.title: “It’s the NFL”: Dak Prescott owns his mistakes after Cowboys’ loss to Buccaneers
articles.standfirst: The offense cannot expect to win games if it fails to capitalize on the opportunities it receives
articles.summary: The offense cannot expect to win games if it fails to capitalize on the opportunities it receives
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys have plenty of reasons to be frustrated with their defense. Allowing 419 total yards, surrendering 241 rushing yards and watching an undrafted rookie quarterback control the football for nearly 40 minutes is hardly a recipe for success. But Dak Prescott isn't interested in using the defense as an excuse.

Following Dallas' 24-16 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Thursday night at AT&T Stadium, the Cowboys quarterback delivered a straightforward assessment of what his team needs to do to turn its season around: score more points.

“Yeah, score. I mean, just honestly score. It's the NFL,” Prescott said when asked what he could do to help the defense. “Their hands are full, and they've got a tough task, and so do we on our side. So at the end of the day, I've got to control what I can control and that's score.” It was a candid admission from the quarterback entrusted with leading Dallas' offense, and it underscored a difficult reality for the Cowboys.

Their defense has struggled to consistently stop opponents, but the offense cannot expect to win games if it fails to capitalize on the opportunities it receives. Prescott knows the standard. If Dallas wants to overcome its defensive shortcomings, its offense must deliver considerably more than 16 points.

Dak Prescott refuses to hide behind the defense

The Cowboys' defensive performance against Tampa Bay provided plenty of ammunition for critics. The Buccaneers controlled possession for 39 minutes and 10 seconds, limiting Dallas' opportunities to get back into the game. Tampa Bay also produced 241 rushing yards, repeatedly exploiting a defense that has struggled to establish consistency.

Two explosive plays accounted for 136 yards and helped transform the game after halftime. Bucky Irving broke loose for a 72-yard run to set up Tampa Bay's opening touchdown drive of the third quarter. On the Buccaneers' next possession, rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels connected with Tez Johnson for a 64-yard completion after cornerback DaRon Bland slipped, leaving the receiver with substantial open space.

Those plays helped Tampa Bay build a 21-10 lead, putting Dallas in a difficult position. Yet Prescott refused to make the defense the primary explanation for the defeat. “I'm a positive guy, and at the end of the day, that was 24 points,” Prescott said. “I mean, we've been scoring 30 points a game. That's on us. That's on us.”

His point was clear. Dallas had established an expectation that its offense could consistently produce enough points to compensate for defensive deficiencies. Against Tampa Bay , it failed to meet that standard.

The Buccaneers entered the game winless, making the defeat even more damaging for a Cowboys team attempting to establish itself as a contender. Rather than taking advantage of an opponent looking for its first victory, Dallas allowed Tampa Bay to dictate the pace and leave with a 24-16 win.

The defense is allowing explosive play

The Dallas Cowboys have a problem that goes beyond their struggling defense: their entire formula for winning is breaking down. Dallas needs its offense to produce points in bunches because its defense cannot consistently stop opponents. But against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, the offense turned the ball over three times, managed just 16 points and failed to sustain drives, leaving the defense on the field for nearly 40 minutes.

That is the contradiction at the heart of the Cowboys’ season. The defense is allowing explosive plays and struggling to get off the field, while the offense is failing to control possession, protect the football and deliver the points needed to compensate. Neither unit is doing enough to cover for the other.

Dak Prescott understands that Dallas cannot expect to win by scoring 16 points and blaming the defense for allowing 24. His responsibility is to make the offense more efficient, limit turnovers and capitalize on scoring opportunities. But the larger challenge belongs to the entire team: the Cowboys must find a way to become competitive on both sides of the ball rather than relying on one unit to rescue the other every week.

Dallas’ central problem is its lack of balance. Until the offense becomes more consistent and the defense becomes more dependable, the Cowboys will remain vulnerable to precisely the kind of defeat they suffered against Tampa Bay. The defense deserves scrutiny. But Prescott understands that the offense has a responsibility to keep the team competitive, especially when stopping opponents consistently has become such a challenge.

articles.title: Dak Prescott reacts to harsh criticism after Cowboys’ latest stumble
articles.standfirst: Dallas lost this week, continuing its “one week on, one week off” pattern.
articles.summary: Dallas lost this week, continuing its “one week on, one week off” pattern.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys are testing their fans’ patience. One week, they give fans reason to believe they can compete for something meaningful. The next, they raise doubts all over again with a loss that seems to erase whatever progress they had made. On Thursday, October 8, Dallas fell 24-16 to the winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers , delivering another performance that was difficult to defend. This time, the frustration even spilled into the AT&T Stadium tunnel, where Dak Prescott faced criticism he did not take particularly well.

As Prescott walked through the tunnel, a stadium worker called the Cowboys’ performance “embarrassing.” Prescott responded by addressing another employee, saying, “You’re real brave. Get him out of here.” Later, during his postgame press conference, the quarterback acknowledged that the man had a right to his opinion and even admitted he might have been right. However, Prescott explained that he was bothered by the worker continuing to make comments while avoiding eye contact with him.

The Cowboys had opportunities to stay in the game , but their mistakes ultimately made any comeback attempt more difficult. In the second half, Bucky Irving broke free for a 72-yard run that helped Tampa Bay take the lead . Later, a pass from Prescott bounced off Ryan Flournoy’s hands and was intercepted by Yaya Diaby. A fumble by KaVontae Turpin then gave the Buccaneers another chance to extend their advantage.

There was still a moment to believe. In the fourth quarter, Prescott led a 99-yard drive and connected with George Pickens on a 13-yard touchdown pass . But just when Dallas needed to capitalize on that momentum, another interception off a deflected pass ended its hopes.

Will the pattern continue?

The Cowboys will visit the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field on Sunday, October 18 , with a chance to shake off the bitter taste of their latest loss. If they maintain the alternating pattern of results they have shown recently, this would be their week to celebrate.

articles.standfirst: The team may already be showing signs of what could happen next.
articles.summary: The team may already be showing signs of what could happen next.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys entered the 2026 season with high expectations and hopes of making a deep playoff run. However, their first five games have left fans with more questions than answers, as the results have swung between excitement and frustration without giving the team a chance to build a winning streak.

Amid these ups and downs, a pattern in their results has caught attention.

Dallas opened the season with a 28-20 loss to the New York Giants in Week 1. Seven days later, the Cowboys responded with a convincing 37-20 win over the Washington Commanders , reigniting their fans' hopes.

But the excitement didn't last long. In Week 3, the Baltimore Ravens edged out Dallas 34-31 . The Cowboys managed to bounce back against the Houston Texans with a 34-30 victory , but they couldn't build on that result to start a winning streak.

The 24-16 loss to Tampa Bay left the Cowboys with three losses and two wins in their first five games , a sequence that raises a new question heading into their next matchup.

If the alternating pattern continues, Dallas would pick up a win in its next game, although previous results don't guarantee the trend will repeat itself. The test comes against the Green Bay Packers on Sunday, October 18, at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wisconsin .
